Joe Biden was much more clearly “a moderate” as a matter of personal identity.

But he embraced Obama’s second term shifts on climate, guns, immigration, and LGBT issues while moving to Obama’s left on education and fiscal issues and adopting weird new antitrust ideas.

The Democratic Party is now a majority liberal party and it will get the kind of nominees and platforms that progressives prefer — but there are still good progressive reasons to prefer Obama-like candidates who pay attention to public opinion and win swing voters.

On energy, Obama espoused an “all of the above” approach and resisted calls to crush the fracking boom in its cradle. 

For all that it is genuinely true that he was progressives’ preferred candidate in the 2008 primary!

On cultural issues, Obama was attentive to public opinion  — he flip-flopped on marriage equality after it became popular, criticized affirmative action in 2008, and was vocally critical of cancel culture.

Obama struck certain economic populist themes just as every Democrat since Roosevelt (or arguably Jefferson) has but he cultivated business allies, talked about fiscal responsibility and was certainly not a socialist.

Synthesis — Obama was on the left of the Iraq debate which was highly salient at the time and made him the preferred candidate of progressives.

But he also behaved very differently from modern progressives!


John Ganz (@lionel_trolling)

Obama did not run as a centrist. He ran as a critic of the Iraq war with a very populist message. He was more the Howard Dean side of the party, which is why he chose Biden as his running mate.
